method: Read-only source audit of React components, global/account/motion CSS, navigation hook and relevant accessibility/navigation/legal/account test sources. No browser execution, member session access or code/git changes. Rendered evidence is owned by root.
instructions: No AGENTS.md found in repository or workspace parent paths. Read frontend-testing-debugging and react-best-practices; followed assigned source-only scope.

findings.title: Account backup import has no visible keyboard focus indicator

evidence.fact: Import label contains the native focusable file input but has account-import-label class, not import-label.
File input covers the label and has opacity:0, so its own focus outline is invisible.
Visible wrapper focus styling only matches .import-label:focus-within; account-import-label has no focus-within or focus-visible styling anywhere in account.css.

findings.impact: A keyboard user reaching account Import workout backup gets an invisible focused file input. The control remains keyboard operable; the problem is focus indication, not missing keyboard activation.
findings.recommendation: Add .account-import-label:focus-within to the visible focus outline rule or give this label the shared import-label class. Verify focus outline is not clipped by wrapper overflow.
findings.validation: In an authorized account fixture, tab from Export my data onto Import workout backup and verify a clearly visible wrapper indicator. No live member data is needed.

findings.status: confirmed_scroll_only_behavior_in_source; conformance impact needs rendered keyboard verification
findings.title: Legal contents navigation scrolls without moving keyboard focus to its section

evidence.fact: Every contents link points to the current route hash, prevents default, then only calls scrollIntoView on a section heading.

findings.impact: Pressing Enter on a contents item visually navigates to a section, but focus remains in the contents list. The next Tab continues through the contents controls rather than from the section just chosen. The link also does not expose a section-specific destination.
findings.recommendation: Keep route hash semantics intact, but give the target heading tabIndex=-1 and focus it after scrolling; choose a route-compatible section navigation scheme if deep links are desired.
findings.validation: On privacy and terms, activate a contents link with Enter, confirm target section focus and subsequent sequential keyboard navigation.
findings.criterion: Focus-order/navigation usability risk; not claimed as a proven WCAG failure without rendered verification.

findings.title: Legal contents explicitly requests smooth scrolling under reduced-motion preference

evidence.fact: Reduced-motion CSS sets scroll-behavior:auto, but an explicit JavaScript smooth request does not rely on the CSS computed scroll behavior.

findings.impact: Users requesting reduced motion still receive animated section scrolling when they use legal contents links. This is a motion-preference inconsistency, not a claim of AA failure.
findings.recommendation: Use matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to select instant/auto versus smooth, or use behavior:auto and let reduced-motion-aware CSS choose scrolling behavior.
findings.validation: With reducedMotion:reduce, activate legal contents links and verify no smooth scrolling; keep ordinary preference navigation functional.
findings.criterion: WCAG SC 2.3.3 is AAA; treat as preference/usability repair, not AA conformance blocker.

existingSafeguards.fact: Native dialog.showModal, title labeling, initial focus, Escape cancel handling, visible close control, Tab wrap and connected opener focus restoration exist.
Closed mobile sidebar is inert; open navigation makes main inert, traps Tab and supports Escape/toggle focus restoration.
All ten routes are recognized; useSyncExternalStore tracks hash, updates document title and focuses main h1 with tabIndex=-1.
Skip-to-content link focuses the page heading; saving status is not repeatedly live-announced.
Reordering uses named native buttons with boundary disabled states; editor fields are labeled; unsaved-discard confirmation receives focus.
Set controls have exercise/set/measurement names and completion pressed states; rest timer uses role=timer rather than an every-second live status.
Compact images are decorative within aria-hidden previews; full guide image has alt text and caption; onLoad/onError end loading and expose fallback text; atlas has stable explicit aspect ratio.
Guide text remains visible when artwork/instruction import fails; full-instruction errors use role=alert; external source links use noopener noreferrer.

Auth fields are wrapped in labels, email/name autocomplete exists, errors are alerts, success messages statuses, progressbar has a label and min/max/current values. Member flows were source reviewed only.
Shared focus outlines, transparent-overlay accessible Settings/Recovery file controls, 48px schedule buttons and global reduced-motion overrides exist.
Training chart numbers/dates are actual text; personal-best table has column and row headers. No source-only claim of inaccessible chart data is justified.

testCoverageNotes.fact: Existing axe WCAG A/AA scans cover seven routes at 1536px/390px and routine, exercise-guide, finish-workout, history-detail/editor dialogs. Account/privacy/terms are not in this scan list. Do not describe all ten routes as axe-audited from this file.
Navigation regression covers a hashchange listener setup race, not legal contents focus or account import focus.

limitations: No screenshots, rendered appearance, actual target spacing, contrast, focus clipping, keyboard run or screen-reader run verified by this audit.
No automatic accessibility test was executed by this worker; root and parallel test worker own current browser/test evidence.
No other supported keyboard, semantic, ARIA, touch or image-loading defect found in inspected source. This is not an assertion of complete accessibility conformance.
